result.rationale: In the diff's GoogleCalendarService updateEvent, the fallback branch is `const selectedCalendar = externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. Since this branch only executes when externalCalendarId is falsy, the find compares cal.externalId against a falsy/undefined value and can never match, so selectedCalendar is undefined — whereas the removed line returned `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. Same defect appears in deleteEvent. Behavior regression is verifiable directly from the diff.

judged_text: In updateEvent the fallback branch evaluates `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)` where externalCalendarId is by definition falsy (that branch only runs when `externalCalendarId ?` failed), so the find compares against undefined and never matches. When a booking reference has no externalCalendarId, selectedCalendar resolves to undefined instead of the previous `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`, so the calendar update is issued against the wrong calendar (or undefined calendarId) and the reschedule silently fails or corrupts the wrong event.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent()`, the fallback branch is `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. That branch only executes when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, so the predicate compares against `undefined` and will not match a normal calendar entry, yielding `selectedCalendar = undefined` (previously it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId` when destinationCalendar was a single object). This can cause the update to target the default/primary calendar (or an undefined calendarId depending on the downstream call), instead of the intended destination calendar, matching the finding’s described failure mode.
